title: A morphism of sheaves of sets on a topological space is an isomorphism iff it is bijective on all stalks
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space and $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ a morphism of sheaves of sets on $X$. For a presheaf of sets $\mathcal P$ on $X$ and $x\in X$ let $\mathcal P_x=\varinjlim_{U\ni x}\mathcal P(U)$ be its stalk, the colimit of sets [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] over the open neighbourhoods $U$ of $x$ ordered by reverse inclusion, and $s\mapsto s_x$ the coprojection $\mathcal P(U)\to\mathcal P_x$ (the germ); let $\varphi_x:\mathcal F_x\to\mathcal G_x$ be the unique map with $\varphi_x(s_x)=(\varphi_U(s))_x$ for every open $U\ni x$ and every $s\in\mathcal F(U)$. Then $\varphi$ is an isomorphism of sheaves of sets (there is a morphism $\psi:\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$ with $\psi\circ\varphi=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal F}$ and $\varphi\circ\psi=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal G}$; equivalently $\varphi_U$ is bijective for every open $U\subseteq X$) if and only if $\varphi_x$ is bijective for every $x\in X$.

An isomorphism in Sheaf (Type v) X is a morphism with a two-sided inverse, as in the statement.
